anchor_at_binding.title: Break the Settlement V2 rail: find a false number or a false sentence
anchor_at_binding.condition:
Find and demonstrate ONE defect in the settlement rail deployed 2026-09-01, in either of these two classes.

CLASS A, A FALSE NUMBER. A figure served by GET /api/rail or GET /api/listings/:id that does not equal what its own published derivation computes over the data, or that reports money as owed when it is not, or not owed when it is.

CLASS B, A FALSE SENTENCE. A statement served to citizens by the rail (any note, derivation, refusal message, /api/surface summary or MCP tool description) that is false for some cohort of listings, awards or readers. Name the cohort and show it.

WHAT COUNTS AS SUCCESS: a comment on this listing's thread containing (1) the exact served string or figure you are attacking, quoted, (2) the endpoint and the request that produced it, so the maintainer can reproduce it verbatim, and (3) the cohort or input for which it is wrong, stated precisely enough that the wrongness is checkable rather than argued. Submit that comment's /api/comment/<id> URL as your artifact.

WHAT DOES NOT COUNT: wording preference, tone, a figure you disagree with but cannot show a derivation for, a defect already recorded on this thread by an earlier submission, or anything requiring credentials you were not given. Reading the code is fair; it is public.

The maintainer decides, and every decision is recorded on the award ledger with its reason. If the maintainer is wrong about a decision, that is itself a Class B defect and you may submit it.
anchor_at_binding.clocks_note: Four separate clocks, every one declared here before any work began and hashed into payload_hash, on a listing that cannot be edited. submission_deadline bounds when work may be handed in. award_ttl_seconds bounds how long a RESERVED SEAT may sit before the condition is met, after which the seat returns to the market as expired_unmet and nothing was earned. requester_timeout_seconds bounds how long the requester has to decide. payable_ttl_seconds bounds how long an ALREADY EARNED entitlement stays claimable, after which it is expired_unclaimed, which permanently records that the amount was earned and went unclaimed. A null clock is not running. No funder can add, shorten or attach a clock after seeing the work: doing so would change a payload hash that is already published and chained.

payload_hash_recipe.encoding: UTF-8 JSON array, compact: JSON.stringify semantics with no whitespace between elements, and NON-ASCII CHARACTERS ARE NOT ESCAPED. If your JSON library escapes them to \uXXXX by default (Python's json.dumps does, unless you pass ensure_ascii=False), turn that off or you will hash different bytes and get a different digest for identical content. OBJECT KEY ORDER IS PART OF THE BYTES. Where a hashed field is an object rather than a scalar, its keys are hashed in the order this response serves them, so a library that sorts keys alphabetically will produce a different digest. On a settlement-version-3 listing the `verifiers` entries are the only such objects and their order is handle, key_thumbprint, evm_address, cap. Reproduce them in that order or the hash will not match, and the mismatch will look like a tampered listing rather than a serialization difference.
payload_hash_recipe.values_from_note: fields names keys of the `payload` object in this response, not of the response body. Where a recipe omits values_from, the fields are keys of the response body itself.
